title: What are the differences between a Stream and a Collection?
keyPoints: A Collection stores elements in memory (eager, reusable, mutable, has size and random access).
A Stream processes elements on demand (lazy, single-use, immutable pipeline, no storage, no size).
Collections use external iteration (you control the loop); streams use internal iteration (stream controls traversal).
Collections are about HAVING data; streams are about PROCESSING data.
Streams cannot modify the source; they produce new streams or results via collect/reduce.
Streams support built-in parallelism via parallelStream(); collection parallelism requires manual threading.
The typical pattern: collection.stream() -> pipeline -> collect() -> back to collection.

s1_definition.oneliner: A Collection stores data (eager, reusable, mutable); a Stream processes data (lazy, single-use, immutable pipeline): Collections hold, Streams flow.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Storage**: Collection stores elements in memory. Stream stores nothing and processes on the fly.
- **Evaluation**: Collection is eager (all elements exist). Stream is lazy (computed on demand).
- **Reuse**: Collection is reusable (iterate many times). Stream is single-use (consumed after terminal).
- **Mutability**: Collection supports add, remove, set. Stream cannot modify the source.
- **Iteration**: Collection uses external iteration (your loop). Stream uses internal iteration (stream controls).
- **Parallelism**: Collection requires manual threading. Stream provides built-in parallelStream().
- **Purpose**: Collection is the data layer. Stream is the computation layer.
s1_definition.analogy: A Collection is the bank vault at National Bank of India: it stores cash physically. You can count it (size), add more, remove some, and visit it multiple times. A Stream is the cash-counting machine: cash flows through it, gets counted, sorted, and filtered, but the machine stores nothing. Once cash passes through, the machine resets. The vault is about HAVING data. The machine is about PROCESSING data.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Collection (stores)            Stream (processes)
  ┌──────────────────┐           ┌──────────────────┐
  │ List<Account>    │ .stream() │ filter(active)   │
  │ size: 3          │─────────→ │ map(balance)     │
  │ get(0): SAV2001  │           │ reduce(add)      │
  │ add, remove, set │           │ = Rs.375000      │
  └──────────────────┘           └──────────────────┘
  Stores data                    Processes data
  Eager, reusable               Lazy, single-use
  Mutable                       Immutable pipeline
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Collections store data: they have size, random access, add, remove, and are reusable. Streams process data: they are lazy, single-use, have no storage, and cannot modify the source.

They work together: Collection stores the data (data layer), Stream processes the data (computation layer). The typical pattern is collection.stream() to pipeline to collect() back to collection.

Remember one sentence: Collections hold data, Streams process data, and they work together with collection.stream() into pipeline into collect().
